title: La discussion académique : exprimer son accord et son désaccord / Academic discussion: expressing agreement and disagreement
bridge: In Spanish, we often introduce our point of view with phrases like 'creo que', 'me parece que', or 'estoy de acuerdo con...'. In French, at this level, a more nuanced and formal range is expected: structures such as 'je suis tout à fait de l'avis de...', 'je ne saurais être plus en désaccord', or 'il me semble que' are used. The main pitfall is the literal calque of 'estoy de acuerdo' as 'je suis d'accord', which works but sounds too simple for a seminar. Another key difference is the use of the subjunctive after expressions of negative opinion or doubt, which also exists in Spanish but is used more systematically in French, especially after phrases like 'il est peu probable que' or 'je ne pense pas que'.
rule: To express agreement and disagreement in an academic seminar in French, you must master several structures depending on the level of formality. 1) Full agreement: 'je suis tout à fait d'accord avec (personne)', 'je partage entièrement l'avis de...', 'je suis du même avis que...'. 2) Partial agreement: 'je suis d'accord dans une certaine mesure', 'je rejoins [personne] sur ce point, mais...'. 3) Polite disagreement: 'je ne suis pas tout à fait d'accord', 'je vois les choses différemment', 'permettez-moi de nuancer votre propos'. For strong disagreement: 'je ne saurais être en désaccord avec vous', 'je m'oppose fermement à cette idée'. Correct use of the subjunctive after negative opinion verbs is crucial: 'je ne pense pas que cette hypothèse soit valable' (subjunctive 'soit'), whereas in affirmative statements the indicative is used: 'je pense que cette hypothèse est valable'. The subjunctive is also used after impersonal expressions such as 'il est peu probable que', 'il est essentiel que', 'il convient que'. To sound formal, connectors like 'en ce qui concerne', 'quant à', 'du point de vue de', 'dans une perspective...' are employed. The use of 'on' instead of 'nous' is typical in spoken register, though in academic seminars 'nous' is preferred for collective stances. Care must be taken with tense agreement in indirect speech: 'Elle a affirmé que la méthodologie était inadéquate' (imperfect). Avoid repetition of 'je pense' by varying with 'je considère', 'j'estime', 'je suis d'avis que'.

concept_examples.text: Je suis tout à fait de l'avis de Madame Dupont concernant l'impact de la mondialisation.
concept_examples.translation: I fully agree with Ms. Dupont regarding the impact of globalization.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi tu.t‿a.fɛ də l‿a.vi də ma.dam dy.pɔ̃ kɔ̃.sɛʁ.nɑ̃ l‿ɛ̃.pakt də la mɔ̃.dja.li.za.sjɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: Je ne saurais être plus en désaccord avec cette interprétation des données.
concept_examples.translation: I could not disagree more with this interpretation of the data.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɔ.ʁɛ ɛtʁ ply ɑ̃ de.za.kɔʁ a.vɛk sɛt ɛ̃.tɛʁ.pʁe.ta.sjɔ̃ de do.ne/

concept_examples.text: Si je comprends bien votre argument, vous semblez ignorer les facteurs socio-économiques.
concept_examples.translation: If I understand your argument correctly, you seem to be ignoring socioeconomic factors.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si ʒə kɔ̃.pʁɑ̃ bjɛ̃ vɔ.tʁ‿aʁ.ʒy.mɑ̃, vu sɑ̃.ble zi.ɲɔ.ʁe le fak.tœʁ sɔ.sjo.e.kɔ.nɔ.mik/

concept_examples.text: Je pense que cette théorie mérite d'être nuancée, car elle repose sur des postulats discutables.
concept_examples.translation: I think this theory deserves to be nuanced, as it is based on questionable postulates.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə sɛt te.ɔ.ʁi me.ʁit d‿ɛtʁ ny.ɑ̃.se, kaʁ ɛl ʁə.poz syʁ de pɔs.ty.la dis.ky.tabl/

common_error.wrong: Je suis d'accord avec vous, mais je pense que votre idée n'est pas correct.
common_error.correct: Je suis d'accord avec vous, mais je pense que votre idée n'est pas juste.
common_error.correct_alt: Je suis d'accord avec vous, mais je considère que votre idée est discutable.
common_error.explanation: The main error is the literal calque from Spanish 'no es correcto' → 'n'est pas correct'. While 'correct' can be used in French, in this academic context it is more precise to say 'n'est pas juste' or 'est discutable'. Additionally, the original sentence uses 'je pense que' followed by the indicative, which is correct because it is an affirmative statement, but if it were negative ('je ne pense pas que'), the subjunctive would be required: 'je ne pense pas que votre idée soit juste'. Another common trap is translating 'estoy de acuerdo' literally as 'je suis d'accord' without varying with more formal expressions like 'je partage votre point de vue' for an academic register.

examples.original: Je partage votre point de vue, mais je voudrais apporter une nuance.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə paʁ.taʒ vɔ.tʁə pwɛ̃ də vy, mɛ ʒə vu.dʁɛ a.pɔʁ.te yn ny.ɑ̃s/
examples.translation: I share your point of view, but I would like to add a nuance.
examples.note: The use of 'partager' is more formal than 'être d'accord', and 'apporter une nuance' is typical in academic discussions.

examples.original: Je suis d'accord dans une certaine mesure, cependant je reste réservé sur certains points.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi da.kɔʁ dɑ̃.z‿yn sɛʁ.tɛn mə.zyʁ, sə.pɑ̃.dɑ̃ ʒə ʁɛst ʁe.zɛʁ.ve syʁ sɛʁ.tɛ̃ pwɛ̃/
examples.translation: I agree to a certain extent; however, I remain reserved on some points.
examples.note: The expression 'dans une certaine mesure' is a way to qualify agreement. 'Rester réservé' is more formal than 'no estar seguro'.

examples.original: Je vous rejoins sur l'importance de la méthodologie, mais j'aurais quelques réserves quant à son application.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vu ʁə.ʒwɛ̃ syʁ l‿ɛ̃.pɔʁ.tɑ̃s də la me.tɔ.do.lɔ.ʒi, mɛ ʒ‿ɔ.ʁɛ kɛl.kə ʁe.zɛʁv kɑ̃ a sɔ̃.n‿a.pli.ka.sjɔ̃/
examples.translation: I agree with you on the importance of methodology, but I would have some reservations regarding its application.
examples.note: The verb 'rejoindre' (to join someone) is common in this context. 'Quant à' introduces the topic with precision.

examples.original: Permettez-moi de ne pas partager votre opinion sur ce point.
examples.phonetic: /pɛʁ.mɛ.te mwa də nə pa paʁ.ta.ʒe vɔ.tʁ‿ɔ.pi.njɔ̃ syʁ sə pwɛ̃/
examples.translation: Allow me to not share your opinion on this point.
examples.note: Use of the structure 'permettre à quelqu'un de + infinitive' in the imperative form for politeness. Disagreement is direct but formal.

examples.original: Je comprends votre raisonnement, mais je ne le trouve pas entièrement convaincant.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə kɔ̃.pʁɑ̃ vɔ.tʁə ʁɛ.zɔn.mɑ̃, mɛ ʒə nə lə tʁuv pa.z‿ɑ̃.tjɛʁ.mɑ̃ kɔ̃.vɛ̃.kɑ̃/
examples.translation: I understand your reasoning, but I do not find it entirely convincing.
examples.note: The verb 'trouver' + adjective (convaincant) is common. The negation 'ne...pas' surrounds the verb, and the indicative is used because it is an affirmative opinion negated, but the subjunctive is not used in the subordinate clause as it is a direct object.

examples.original: Je ne saurais accepter cette conclusion sans discussion préalable.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɔ.ʁɛ ak.sɛp.te sɛt kɔ̃.kly.zjɔ̃ sɑ̃ dis.ky.sjɔ̃ pʁe.a.labl/
examples.translation: I could not accept this conclusion without prior discussion.
examples.note: The conditional 'saurais' (from 'savoir') in the negative form expresses a polite impossibility. It is a very formal structure.

levels.label: Utiliser le subjonctif après les opinions négatives
levels.translation: Using the subjunctive after negative opinions

examples.original: Je ne pense pas que cette approche soit pertinente dans ce contexte.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sɛt a.pʁɔʃ swa pɛʁ.ti.nɑ̃t dɑ̃ sə kɔ̃.tɛkst/
examples.translation: I do not think this approach is relevant in this context.
examples.note: After 'je ne pense pas que', the subjunctive ('soit') is used. It is a common mistake to use the indicative ('est').

examples.original: Il est peu probable que les résultats soient significatifs avec un échantillon aussi réduit.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛ pø pʁɔ.ba.blə kə le ʁe.zyl.ta swa si.ɲi.fi.ka.tif a.vɛk œ̃.n‿e.ʃɑ̃.ti.jɔ̃ o.si ʁe.dɥi/
examples.translation: It is unlikely that the results will be significant with such a small sample.
examples.note: The impersonal expression 'il est peu probable que' requires the subjunctive. Note the agreement of 'soient' with 'résultats' (plural).

examples.original: Je doute fortement que cette hypothèse explique le phénomène observé.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə dut fɔʁ.tə.mɑ̃ kə sɛ.t‿i.pɔ.tɛz ɛk.splik lə fe.nɔ.mɛn ɔp.sɛʁ.ve/
examples.translation: I strongly doubt that this hypothesis explains the observed phenomenon.
examples.note: The verb 'douter' followed by 'que' requires the subjunctive. In Spanish, the subjunctive is also used ('dudo que explique'), but in French it is mandatory. Here, 'explique' is present subjunctive.

title: Nuancer et argumenter en contexte professionnel / Nuancing and arguing in a professional context
bridge: In Spanish, we often use 'pero', 'sin embargo', 'aunque' to nuance and contradict. In French, for a high-level professional register, mastering the alternation between 'cependant', 'néanmoins', 'toutefois' and 'en revanche' is crucial, as they are not interchangeable: 'en revanche' introduces a parallel contrast, while 'néanmoins' concedes something. Additionally, the use of the subjunctive after 'bien que' and 'quoique' is mandatory, unlike in Spanish where the indicative is sometimes used. Beware of the trap of always translating 'aunque' as 'bien que' in formal contexts: 'encore que' is more elegant but requires the subjunctive.
rule:
In professional French, to nuance an opinion or argue, connectors requiring specific verb moods are used:
- **Cependant, néanmoins, toutefois** (however, nevertheless) are followed by the indicative. They are placed at the beginning of the sentence or after the main verb.
- **En revanche** (on the other hand, by contrast) introduces a contrast, with the indicative.
- **Bien que, quoique, encore que** (although, even though) require the subjunctive, even if the fact is real. 'Encore que' is formal and often used as an aside at the end.
- **Certes... mais** (certainly... but) is a typical argumentation structure: 'Certes, le budget est limité, mais nous pouvons optimiser.'
- To concede and counter: 'Il est vrai que... Cependant...'. Nuance is achieved with adverbs like 'peut-être', 'probablement', 'assurément'.
- Caution: in French, 'si' (even though) with the subjunctive is very formal and literary.
- In negotiation, impersonal structures are used: 'Il serait envisageable de...' (it would be feasible to...), 'Il convient de noter que...' (it is worth noting that...).

concept_examples.text: Le projet est ambitieux ; néanmoins, les délais semblent réalisables.
concept_examples.translation: The project is ambitious; nevertheless, the deadlines seem feasible.
concept_examples.phonetic: /lə pʁɔʒɛ ɛt‿ɑ̃bisjø ; neɑ̃mwɑ̃, le dəlɛ sɑ̃bl ʁeazab/

concept_examples.text: Bien que les résultats soient positifs, il faut rester prudent.
concept_examples.translation: Although the results are positive, one must remain cautious.
concept_examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə le ʁezylta swa pɔzitif, il fo ʁɛste pʁydɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: En revanche, notre équipe a gagné en efficacité.
concept_examples.translation: On the other hand, our team has gained in efficiency.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ ʁəvɑ̃ʃ, nɔtʁ ekip a gaɲe ɑ̃ efikasite/

concept_examples.text: Certes, le coût est élevé, mais la qualité justifie cet investissement.
concept_examples.translation: Admittedly, the cost is high, but the quality justifies this investment.
concept_examples.phonetic: /sɛʁt, lə ku ɛt‿elève, mɛ la kalite ʒystifi sɛt‿ɛ̃vɛstismɑ̃/

common_error.wrong: Bien que les résultats sont positifs, il faut rester prudent.
common_error.correct: Bien que les résultats soient positifs, il faut rester prudent.
common_error.correct_alt: Encore que les résultats soient positifs, il faut rester prudent.
common_error.explanation: The typical error is using the indicative after 'bien que' because in Spanish 'aunque' is often constructed with the indicative. In French, the conjunctions 'bien que', 'quoique' and 'encore que' always require the subjunctive. To avoid this, remember that these conjunctions express a concession, and the subjunctive is mandatory even if the fact is true. Practice with irregular verbs like 'être' (soit), 'avoir' (ait) and 'faire' (fasse).

examples.original: Bien que le marché soit instable, nous maintenons nos prévisions.
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə lə maʁʃe swa ɛ̃stabl, nu mɛ̃tənɔ̃ no pʁevizjɔ̃/
examples.translation: Although the market may be unstable, we maintain our forecasts.
examples.note: Subjunctive 'soit' after 'bien que'. In Spanish, the indicative can be used, but in French the subjunctive is always required.

examples.original: Quoique les chiffres aient chuté, l'entreprise reste confiante.
examples.phonetic: /kwak le ʃifʁ ɛt‿ʃyte, lɑ̃tʁəpʁiz ʁɛst kɔ̃fjɑ̃t/
examples.translation: Even though the figures have dropped, the company remains confident.
examples.note: 'Quoique' is more formal than 'bien que'. 'aient' is the subjunctive of 'avoir'.

examples.original: Encore que cette décision soit difficile, elle est nécessaire.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃kɔʁ kə sɛt desizjɔ̃ swa difisil, ɛl ɛt nesesɛʁ/
examples.translation: Even though this decision may be difficult, it is necessary.
examples.note: 'Encore que' is elegant and used in very formal registers. It requires the subjunctive.

examples.original: Cependant, il faut tenir compte des contraintes budgétaires.
examples.phonetic: /səpɑ̃dɑ̃, il fo təniʁ kɔ̃t de kɔ̃tʁɛ̃t bydʒetɛʁ/
examples.translation: However, one must take budget constraints into account.
examples.note: 'Cependant' is used at the beginning or in a pause. It does not require the subjunctive.

examples.original: Les ventes sont stables ; leurs marges, en revanche, diminuent.
examples.phonetic: /le vɑ̃t sɔ̃ stabil ; lœʁ maʁʒ, ɑ̃ ʁəvɑ̃ʃ, diminɥ/
examples.translation: Sales are stable; their margins, on the other hand, are decreasing.
examples.note: 'En revanche' contrasts two parallel aspects. In Spanish, it is equivalent to 'en cambio'.

examples.original: Toutefois, cette approche pourrait être risquée à long terme.
examples.phonetic: /tut fwa, sɛt apʁɔʃ puʁɛ ɛtʁ ʁiske a lɔ̃ tɛʁm/
examples.translation: Nonetheless, this approach could be risky in the long term.
examples.note: 'Toutefois' is synonymous with 'cependant' but sounds more formal. Often used after a period.

examples.original: Néanmoins, nous devons admettre que nos concurrents sont plus rapides.
examples.phonetic: /neɑ̃mwɛ̃, nu dəvɔ̃ admɛtʁ kə no kɔ̃kyʁɑ̃ sɔ̃ ply ʁapid/
examples.translation: Nevertheless, we must admit that our competitors are faster.
examples.note: 'Néanmoins' implies a concession. Useful in negotiations.

examples.original: Certes, le plan A est solide, mais il présente des risques opérationnels.
examples.phonetic: /sɛʁt, lə plɑ̃ a ɛt sɔlid, mɛ il pʁezɑ̃t de ʁisk ɔpeʁasjɔnɛl/
examples.translation: Admittedly, Plan A is solid, but it presents operational risks.
examples.note: The 'Certes... mais...' structure is key for conceding and then objecting.

examples.original: Il est vrai que la formation exige du temps ; cependant, elle améliore la productivité.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛt vʁɛ kə la fɔʁmasjɔ̃ ɛgziʒ dy tɑ̃ ; səpɑ̃dɑ̃, ɛl ameliɔʁ la pʁodyktivite/
examples.translation: It is true that training requires time; however, it improves productivity.
examples.note: This construction is typical in reports and presentations. With 'il est vrai que' one concedes, then contradicts with 'cependant'.

examples.original: Si les délais sont courts, nous pouvons néanmoins livrer dans deux mois.
examples.phonetic: /si le dəlɛ sɔ̃ kuʁ, nu puvɔ̃ neɑ̃mwɛ̃ livʁe dɑ̃ dø mwa/
examples.translation: If the deadlines are short, we can nonetheless deliver in two months.
examples.note: Use of 'si' conditional + 'néanmoins' to nuance. Do not confuse with concession.

examples.original: Nous devons réduire les coûts sans compromettre la qualité ; autrement dit, il faut innover.
examples.phonetic: /nu dəvɔ̃ ʁedɥiʁ le ku sɑ̃ kɔ̃pʁɔmɛtʁ la kalite ; otʁəmɑ̃ di, il fo inɔve/
examples.translation: We must reduce costs without compromising quality; in other words, we need to innovate.
examples.note: Connectors like 'autrement dit' (in other words) help reformulate and clarify.

title: Analyse littéraire et culturelle / Literary and Cultural Analysis
bridge: When analyzing literature and culture, formal French uses structures that have no direct equivalent in Spanish: subject-verb inversion for stylistic emphasis, the expletive 'ne', and discourse connectors like 'dès lors' or 'pour ainsi dire'. Spanish tends to use passive voice ('se considera') or verbal periphrases, while French prefers active voice and impersonal constructions such as 'il apparaît que'. Avoid calquing 'en tanto que' (in Spanish) as 'en tant que' (in French) when you simply mean 'como' with a causal value; French requires 'comme' or 'puisque'. Be careful with the order of combined pronouns, which differs from Spanish: 'il me le montre' versus 'me lo muestra'.
rule: For literary analysis in French at C1 level, master: (1) complex inversion (subject-verb) after adverbs like 'peut-être', 'apparemment', with or without expletive 'ne': 'Peut-être faudrait-il considérer…'; (2) the subjunctive after expressions of negated opinion or doubt: 'Je ne pense pas que cette interprétation soit valable', 'Bien que l’auteur utilise…' → subjunctive; (3) argumentative connectors: 'en outre', 'd’une part … d’autre part', 'en définitive', 'dès lors' (therefore), 'ainsi' (thus), 'en effet' (indeed, which does not always equal 'en efecto'); (4) nominalizations: 'la relecture de ce mythe', 'le dépassement du réalisme'; (5) the use of 'ce qui/ce que' and 'c’est … qui/que' for emphasis. Do not use the future subjunctive (non-existent in French). Remember that the passé simple (used in narration) alternates with the imparfait: 'L’auteur écrivit son chef-d’œuvre en 1862, mais il y travaillait déjà depuis dix ans'. Exception: the subject 'on' never allows stylistic inversion; with impersonal 'il' ('il faut lire') inversion does not occur in formal register.

concept_examples.text: Peut-être faut-il considérer cette œuvre comme une critique implicite de la société.
concept_examples.translation: Perhaps one must consider this work as an implicit critique of society.
concept_examples.phonetic: pə.tɛːʁ fo.t‿il kɔ̃.si.de.ʁe sɛt‿œvʁ kɔm yn kʁi.tik ɛ̃.pli.sit də la sɔ.sje.te

concept_examples.text: Bien que le roman soit ancré dans le XIXe siècle, ses thèmes restent universels.
concept_examples.translation: Although the novel is rooted in the 19th century, its themes remain universal.
concept_examples.phonetic: bjɛ̃ kə lə ʁɔ.mɑ̃ swa ɑ̃.kʁe dɑ̃ lə diz.nœ.vjɛm sjɛk.lə, se tɛm ʁɛst y.ni.vɛʁ.sɛl

concept_examples.text: Dès lors, on comprend pourquoi l’auteur privilégie le point de vue interne.
concept_examples.translation: From then on, one understands why the author favors the internal point of view.
concept_examples.phonetic: dɛ lɔʁ, ɔ̃ kɔ̃.pʁɑ̃ puʁ.kwa l‿o.tœʁ pʁi.vi.le.ʒi lə pwɛ̃ də vɥ ɛ̃.tɛʁn

concept_examples.text: C’est cette tension entre le réel et le symbolique qui donne au texte sa profondeur.
concept_examples.translation: It is this tension between the real and the symbolic that gives the text its depth.
concept_examples.phonetic: s‿ɛ sɛt tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ ɑ̃tʁ lə ʁe.ɛl e lə sɛ̃.bɔ.lik ki dɔn o tɛkst sa pʁɔ.fɔ̃.dœʁ

common_error.wrong: Je ne pense pas que cette interprétation est valable, parce que l’auteur a utilisé l’ironie.
common_error.correct: Je ne pense pas que cette interprétation soit valable, parce que l’auteur a utilisé l’ironie.
common_error.correct_alt: Je ne pense pas que cette interprétation soit valable, car l’auteur a eu recours à l’ironie.
common_error.explanation: The error lies in using the indicative ('est') after 'ne pense pas que' (negation of opinion)—French requires the subjunctive ('soit'). In Spanish, the indicative is sometimes used colloquially ('creo que es válida', 'no creo que es válida'), but the subjunctive is preferred. Additionally, 'parce que' expresses direct cause, but in academic register 'car' (more formal) or 'puisque' (known cause) are preferred. To avoid the error: memorize that 'ne pas penser que' + subjunctive, just like 'douter que', 'nier que'.

examples.original: Peut-être convient-il de distinguer l’auteur du narrateur.
examples.phonetic: pə.tɛːʁ kɔ̃.vjɛ̃.t‿il də dis.tɛ̃.ɡe l‿o.tœʁ dy na.ʁa.tœʁ
examples.translation: Perhaps one should distinguish the author from the narrator.
examples.note: Complex inversion is mandatory after 'peut-être' in formal writing. Do not say 'peut-être il convient' in formal writing.

examples.original: À peine le lecteur a-t-il refermé le livre que la réflexion commence.
examples.phonetic: a pɛn lə lɛk.tœʁ a t‿il ʁə.fɛʁ.me lə livʁ kə la ʁe.flɛk.sjɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃s
examples.translation: Hardly has the reader closed the book when reflection begins.
examples.note: With 'à peine', the subject is inverted and the euphonic 't' is added. Spanish uses 'apenas... cuando' without inversion.

examples.original: À quoi tient, selon vous, la puissance évocatrice de ce poème ?
examples.phonetic: a kwa tjɛ̃, sə.lɔ̃ vu, la pɥi.sɑ̃s e.vɔ.ka.tʁis də sə pɔ.ɛm
examples.translation: What, in your view, accounts for the evocative power of this poem?
examples.note: Complex interrogative with subject inversion and placement of the adverb 'selon vous'.

examples.original: Il est peu probable que le narrateur soit fiable, tant ses descriptions sont subjectives.
examples.phonetic: il ɛ pø pʁɔ.ba.blə kə lə na.ʁa.tœʁ swa fja.blə, tɑ̃ se dɛs.kʁip.sjɔ̃ sɔ̃ syb.ʒɛk.tiv
examples.translation: It is unlikely that the narrator is reliable, given that his descriptions are subjective.
examples.note: The subjunctive is required after 'peu probable que'. 'Tant' introduces the justificatory cause.

examples.original: Quoi que l’on dise, cette œuvre majeure est empreinte de pessimisme.
examples.phonetic: kwa kə l‿ɔ̃ diz, sɛt‿œvʁ ma.ʒœʁ ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.pʁɛ̃t də pe.si.mism
examples.translation: Say what you will, this major work is steeped in pessimism.
examples.note: The phrase 'quoi que' requires the subjunctive. In Spanish, 'aunque' or 'por más que' are used.

examples.original: Bien que certains critiques y aient vu une satire, le roman demeure un hymne à la vie.
examples.phonetic: bjɛ̃ kə sɛʁ.tɛ̃ kʁi.tik i ɛ vu yn sa.tiʁ, lə ʁɔ.mɑ̃ də.mœʁ œ̃.n‿imn a la vi
examples.translation: Although some critics have seen it as satire, the novel remains a hymn to life.
examples.note: With 'bien que', the subjunctive is always used. The passé composé of the subjunctive ('aient vu') is used for prior action.

levels.label: Les connecteurs argumentatifs et la nominalisation

examples.original: D’une part, l’œuvre s’inscrit dans un contexte historique précis ; d’autre part, elle transcende son époque.
examples.phonetic: d‿yn paʁ, l‿œvʁ s‿ɛ̃s.kʁi dɑ̃.z‿œ̃ kɔ̃.tɛkst i.stɔ.ʁik pʁe.si ; d‿o.tʁə paʁ, ɛl tʁɑ̃.sɑ̃d sɔ.n‿e.pɔk
examples.translation: On the one hand, the work is rooted in a precise historical context; on the other, it transcends its era.
examples.note: Correlative structure of connectors: 'd’une part ... d’autre part'. Avoid literal 'por un lado' translation 'd’un côté' (which also exists but is less academic).

examples.original: L’analyse des symboles révèle une tension sous-jacente entre l’ordre et le chaos.
examples.phonetic: l‿a.na.liz de sɛ̃.bɔl ʁe.vɛl yn tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ su.ʒa.sɑ̃t ɑ̃tʁ l‿ɔʁdʁ e lə ka.o
examples.translation: The analysis of the symbols reveals an underlying tension between order and chaos.
examples.note: Nominalization ('l’analyse de') allows for condensation of actions. In Spanish, the infinitive ('analizar') is used, but French prefers the noun at C1 level.

examples.original: En définitive, c’est moins la chute du personnage que sa rédemption qui importe.
examples.phonetic: ɑ̃ de.fi.ni.tiv, s‿ɛ mwɛ̃ la ʃyt dy pɛʁ.sɔ.naʒ kə sa ʁe.dɑ̃p.sjɔ̃ ki ɛ̃.pɔʁt
examples.translation: In the end, what matters less is the character’s downfall than his redemption.
examples.note: The construction 'moins ... que' compares values, and 'c’est ... qui' emphasizes the logical subject. Be careful: do not say 'es menos que' but 'c’est moins ... que'.

title: La nuance et le raisonnement abstrait / Nuance and abstract reasoning
bridge: In Spanish, we tend to use constructions like 'es que' or 'lo que pasa es que' to add nuance. In French, precision in abstract reasoning is achieved through the use of logical connectors (or, donc, par conséquent, en effet), nominalization (le fait que, la possibilité que), and the choice of subjunctive or indicative after expressions of opinion. A common mistake is to translate 'aunque' literally as 'bien que' (always followed by the subjunctive) or to confuse 'car' (causal) with 'parce que' (explanatory). You should also pay attention to the use of the conditional for politeness and the expression of hypotheses with 'si + imparfait' vs. 'si + plus-que-parfait'.
rule: For abstract reasoning in French at the C1 level, it is essential to master: (1) Logical connectors and nuance markers: 'or' (however, to introduce an objection), 'en effet' (indeed), 'par conséquent' (consequently), 'toutefois' (however), 'néanmoins' (nevertheless), 'd'ailleurs' (for that matter). (2) Nominalization with 'le fait que' followed by the subjunctive (though in formal registers the indicative is accepted when the fact is certain, but at C1 level the subjunctive is preferred). (3) The subjunctive after expressions of doubt, necessity, or evaluation: 'il est important que', 'il se peut que', 'je ne pense pas que' (with subjunctive) vs. 'je pense que' (with indicative). (4) Hypotheses and conditions: 'si + imparfait' for present/future hypotheses, 'si + plus-que-parfait' for past hypotheses (do not use 'si + conditionnel' in the protasis). (5) The conditional for politeness and uncertainty: 'je voudrais', 'il faudrait', 'on pourrait'. (6) The expression of cause and consequence: 'car' (cause perceived as evident), 'parce que' (real cause), 'donc', 'ainsi', 'de ce fait'. (7) The use of 'ne explétif' after certain verbs (craindre que + ne, éviter que + ne) in formal registers.

concept_examples.text: Or, il ne faut pas confondre liberté et licence.
concept_examples.translation: However, one must not confuse freedom and libertinism.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɔʁ il nə fo pa kɔ̃fɔ̃dʁ libɛʁte e lisɑ̃s/

concept_examples.text: Le fait qu'il soit opposé à ce projet ne nous empêche pas de poursuivre.
concept_examples.translation: The fact that he opposes this project does not prevent us from continuing.
concept_examples.phonetic: /lə fɛ kɛl swa ɔpoze a sə pʁɔʒɛ nə nu ɑ̃pɛʃ pa də puʁsɥivʁ/

concept_examples.text: Si l'on considère la question sous un angle éthique, la réponse diffère.
concept_examples.translation: If we consider the question from an ethical standpoint, the answer differs.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si lɔ̃ kɔ̃sidɛʁ la kɛstjɔ̃ suz‿œ̃ ɑ̃ɡl etik la ʁepɔ̃s difɛʁ/

concept_examples.text: Il serait souhaitable que chacun prenne conscience de ses responsabilités.
concept_examples.translation: It would be desirable for everyone to become aware of their responsibilities.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il sɛʁe swetabl kə ʃakœ̃ pʁɛn kɔ̃sjɑ̃s də se ʁɛspɔ̃sabilite/

common_error.wrong: Bien que je suis fatigué, je vais continuer.
common_error.correct: Bien que je sois fatigué, je vais continuer.
common_error.correct_alt: Même si je suis fatigué, je vais continuer.
common_error.explanation: The error lies in using the indicative after 'bien que' (which means 'although'). In French, 'bien que' always requires the subjunctive. Spanish speakers tend to use the indicative because in Spanish 'aunque' can take the indicative if the fact is presented as real. To express the same idea with the indicative, you can use 'même si' (which does take the indicative and is equivalent to 'aunque' with a factual concessive value). Avoid literal translation and remember: 'bien que' + subjunctive, 'même si' + indicative.

examples.original: Il prétend être rationnel, or ses arguments sont irrecevables.
examples.phonetic: /il pʁetɑ̃ ɛtʁ ʁasjɔnɛl ɔʁ se zaʁɡymɑ̃ sɔ̃ iʁsəvabl/
examples.translation: He claims to be rational; however, his arguments are unacceptable.
examples.note: 'Or' does not mean 'or' (disjunction), but introduces an objection or new information that contradicts what was said before. It is typical of formal registers.

examples.original: Il n'a pas abouti à une conclusion satisfaisante; en effet, son raisonnement partait d'un postulat erroné.
examples.phonetic: /il n‿a pa z‿abuti a yn kɔ̃klyzjɔ̃ satisfɛzɑ̃t ɑ̃n‿efɛ sɔ̃ ʁɛzɔnmɑ̃ paʁtɛ dœ̃ pɔstyla eʁɔne/
examples.translation: He did not reach a satisfactory conclusion; indeed, his reasoning was based on a flawed postulate.
examples.note: 'En effet' introduces confirmation or explanation of what was said; it differs from 'en fait' which expresses opposition (in fact).

examples.original: Néanmoins, on ne saurait ignorer les conséquences pratiques.
examples.phonetic: /neɑ̃mwɛ̃ ɔ̃ nə sɔʁɛ iɲɔʁe le kɔ̃sekɑ̃s pʁatik/
examples.translation: Nevertheless, one could not ignore the practical consequences.
examples.note: 'Néanmoins' is a formal concessive; it conveys a stronger objection than 'cependant'. 'Saurait' is the conditional of 'savoir' in formal style.

examples.original: Je doute fort qu'il ait compris la nuance du propos.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə dut fɔʁ k‿il ɛ kɔ̃pʁi la nyɑ̃s dy pʁopo/
examples.translation: I strongly doubt that he understood the nuance of the comment.
examples.note: After 'douter' (affirmative), the subjunctive is used; remember that 'douter que' governs the subjunctive, while 'ne pas douter que' can take the indicative or subjunctive.

examples.original: Il se peut que l'éthique et la morale ne coïncident pas toujours.
examples.phonetic: /il sə pø kə letik e la mɔʁal nə kɔɛ̃sid pa tuʒuʁ/
examples.translation: It is possible that ethics and morality do not always coincide.
examples.note: 'Il se peut que' requires the subjunctive; it is a more formal way to express possibility than 'peut-être'.

examples.original: Il n'est pas certain que le libre arbitre soit une illusion.
examples.phonetic: /il n‿ɛ pa sɛʁtɛ̃ kə lə libʁ aʁbitʁ swa yn ijyzjɔ̃/
examples.translation: It is not certain that free will is an illusion.
examples.note: Expressions of doubt like 'il n'est pas certain que' take the subjunctive; so do 'il est peu probable que'.

examples.original: Je ne prétends pas que sa démonstration soit parfaite.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə pʁetɑ̃ pa kə sa demɔ̃stʁasjɔ̃ swa paʁfɛt/
examples.translation: I do not claim that his demonstration is perfect.
examples.note: 'Prétendre que' in the negative requires the subjunctive; in the affirmative, it takes the indicative. This is a subtle nuance that Spanish speakers often overlook.

examples.original: Si l'on admettait que la raison prime sur l'émotion, le débat serait plus serein.
examples.phonetic: /si lɔ̃ admɛtɛ kə la ʁɛzɔ̃ pʁim syʁ lemɔsjɔ̃ lə deba sɛʁɛ ply səʁɛ̃/
examples.translation: If we were to admit that reason prevails over emotion, the debate would be more serene.
examples.note: Hypotheses in the present/future: si + imparfait, conditional in the main clause. Do not use 'si + conditionnel' in the protasis.

examples.original: À supposer qu'il ait dit la vérité, que faudrait-il en conclure ?
examples.phonetic: /a sypoze k‿il ɛ di la veʁite kə fɔdʁɛ il ɑ̃ kɔ̃klyʁ/
examples.translation: Assuming he told the truth, what would we have to conclude?
examples.note: The phrase 'à supposer que' requires the subjunctive and introduces a more theoretical hypothesis. In Spanish we would say 'suponiendo que' with the subjunctive, but be careful with the literal translation of 'que'.

examples.original: Sans les travaux de Kant, la philosophie moderne n'aurait pas la même portée.
examples.phonetic: /sɑ̃ le tʁavo də kɑ̃t la filɔzɔfi mɔdɛʁn n‿ɔʁɛ pa la mɛm pɔʁte/
examples.translation: Without Kant's works, modern philosophy would not have the same scope.
examples.note: Conditions can be expressed with 'sans + noun', without needing a 'si' clause. This is more concise and elegant.

examples.original: Quoi qu'il en soit, il serait malhonnête de nier l'évidence.
examples.phonetic: /kwa k‿il ɑ̃ swa il sɛʁɛ malɔnɛt də nje levidɑ̃s/
examples.translation: Be that as it may, it would be dishonest to deny the evidence.
examples.note: 'Quoi qu'il en soit' is a fixed concessive phrase with the subjunctive; it is the equivalent of 'be that as it may' in English, useful for introducing a conclusion.

title: Le commentaire socio-politique / The sociopolitical commentary
bridge: In French, sociopolitical commentary relies on formal register and modal nuances that often have no direct equivalent in Spanish. While Spanish frequently uses the subjunctive to express hypotheses or concessions, French at C1 level employs structures such as the conditionnel passé, the subjonctif imparfait (in highly formal registers) and logical connectors like 'encore que' or 'dès lors que'. Be careful not to translate 'aunque' literally as 'bien que' + indicative (incorrect; requires subjunctive) or to use 'si' with conditional (forbidden in French).
rule: To comment on current sociopolitical affairs in French at C1 level, master these resources: 1) The conditionnel présent and passé for hypotheses and possibilities (e.g. 'On pourrait croire que...' / 'Il aurait fallu réagir'). 2) The subjunctive after concessive phrases: 'bien que', 'encore que', 'sans que' (always with subjunctive). 3) The indicative after 'parce que', 'puisque', 'comme' (real cause). 4) Connectors of opposition and nuance: 'certes... mais', 'en revanche', 'néanmoins', 'toutefois'. 5) The gerund to express simultaneous actions ('tout en reconnaissant'). Avoid anglicisms and colloquial registers in formal contexts. Tense agreement: in indirect speech, the future becomes conditionnel passé (e.g. 'Il a annoncé qu'il viendrait').

concept_examples.text: Bien que le gouvernement ait promis des réformes, la tension sociale demeure.
concept_examples.translation: Although the government has promised reforms, social tension persists.
concept_examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə lə ɡuvɛʁnəmɑ̃ ɛ pʁɔmi de ʁəfɔʁm, la tɑ̃sjɔ̃ sɔsjal dəmyʁ/

concept_examples.text: On pourrait croire que la crise est derrière nous, mais les chiffres disent le contraire.
concept_examples.translation: We might think the crisis is behind us, but the figures say otherwise.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ pɔ̃tʁe kʁwaʁ kə la kʁiz ɛ dɛʁjɛʁ nu, mɛ le ʃifʁ diz lə kɔ̃tʁɛʁ/

concept_examples.text: Il aurait fallu anticiper les conséquences de cette politique avant de la mettre en œuvre.
concept_examples.translation: We should have anticipated the consequences of this policy before implementing it.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɔʁɛ faly ɑ̃tisipe le kɔ̃sekɑ̃s də sɛt pɔlitik avɑ̃ də la mɛtʁ ɑ̃ œvʁ/

concept_examples.text: Certes, la croissance est en hausse, mais elle profite surtout aux plus aisés.
concept_examples.translation: Admittedly, growth is on the rise, but it mainly benefits the better-off.
concept_examples.phonetic: /sɛʁt, la kʁwasɑ̃s ɛt ɑ̃ ɔs, mɛ ɛl pʁɔfit syʁtu o plyz‿eze/

common_error.wrong: Bien que le gouvernement a promis des réformes, la situation ne change pas.
common_error.correct: Bien que le gouvernement ait promis des réformes, la situation ne change pas.
common_error.correct_alt: Le gouvernement a promis des réformes, mais la situation ne change pas.
common_error.explanation: A typical error for Spanish speakers is using the indicative after 'bien que' because in Spanish 'aunque' often takes the indicative (aunque el gobierno ha prometido). However, 'bien que' always requires the subjunctive in French (ait promis). If you want to use the indicative, change the structure: use 'mais' or 'cependant'. To avoid the error, remember: concessive phrases like 'bien que', 'encore que', 'quoique' take the subjunctive; the alternative is to use 'mais' with the indicative.

examples.original: On pourrait interpréter ce scrutin comme un rejet des élites.
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ pɔ̃tʁe ɛ̃tɛʁpʁete sə skʁytɛ̃ kɔm œ̃ ʁəʒɛ de zelit/
examples.translation: We might interpret this vote as a rejection of the elites.
examples.note: Use of the conditional for politeness and speculation in political commentary.

examples.original: Cette mesure aurait des effets bénéfiques sur l'emploi.
examples.phonetic: /sɛt məzyʁ ɔʁɛ de zɛfɛ benefik syʁ lɑ̃plwa/
examples.translation: This measure would have beneficial effects on employment.
examples.note: The conditional expresses an unconfirmed hypothesis, as in Spanish 'tendría'.

examples.original: Sans le soutien des syndicats, la réforme serait vouée à l'échec.
examples.phonetic: /sɑ̃ lə sutjɛ̃ de sɛ̃dika, la ʁefɔʁm səʁɛ vwe a leʃɛk/
examples.translation: Without the support of the unions, the reform would be doomed to failure.
examples.note: Conditional structure with 'sans' + present conditional.

examples.original: Encore que le bilan soit mitigé, on ne peut nier certains progrès.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃kɔʁ kə lə bilɑ̃ swa mitiʒe, ɔ̃ nø pø nje sɛʁtɛ̃ pʁɔɡʁɛ/
examples.translation: Although the balance sheet is mixed, we cannot deny certain progress.
examples.note: 'Encore que' is more formal than 'bien que' and also requires the subjunctive.

examples.original: Tout en reconnaissant les efforts du gouvernement, les manifestants maintiennent la pression.
examples.phonetic: /tu ɑ̃ ʁəkɔnɛsɑ̃ le zɛfɔʁ dy ɡuvɛʁnəmɑ̃, le manifɛstɑ̃ mɛ̃tjɛn la pʁɛsjɔ̃/
examples.translation: While acknowledging the government's efforts, the protesters maintain pressure.
examples.note: Use of the gerund 'tout en' to express concession, with no direct equivalent in Spanish.

examples.original: Quoique les sondages annoncent une victoire, la réalité du terrain reste incertaine.
examples.phonetic: /kwak le sɔ̃daʒ anɔ̃s yn viktwaʁ, la ʁealite dy tɛʁɛ̃ ʁɛst ɛ̃sɛʁtɛn/
examples.translation: Although polls predict a victory, the reality on the ground remains uncertain.
examples.note: 'Quoique' + subjunctive in French; in Spanish the indicative is often used, but here the subjunctive is required.

levels.label: Analyser les causes et les conséquences

examples.original: Dès lors que la confiance est rompue, le dialogue politique devient impossible.
examples.phonetic: /dɛ lɔʁ kə la kɔ̃fjɑ̃s ɛ ʁɔ̃py, lə djalɔɡ pɔlitik dəvjɛ̃ ɛ̃pɔsibl/
examples.translation: Once trust is broken, political dialogue becomes impossible.
examples.note: 'Dès lors que' introduces a cause that conditions the consequence, similar to 'una vez que' in Spanish.

examples.original: Cette décision résulte d'un compromis entre les partis, ce qui explique son caractère ambigu.
examples.phonetic: /sɛt desizjɔ̃ ʁezylt dɛ̃ kɔ̃pʁɔmi ɑ̃tʁ le paʁti, sə ki ɛksplik sɔ̃ kaʁaktɛʁ ɑ̃biɡy/
examples.translation: This decision results from a compromise between parties, which explains its ambiguous nature.
examples.note: Use of 'ce qui' to refer to the entire previous sentence, very common in political discourse.

examples.original: À force de reporter les réformes, le gouvernement a fini par perdre la confiance des citoyens.
examples.phonetic: /a fɔʁs də ʁəpɔʁte le ʁefɔʁm, lə ɡuvɛʁnəmɑ̃ a fini paʁ pɛʁdʁ la kɔ̃fjɑ̃s de sitwajɛ̃/
examples.translation: By repeatedly postponing reforms, the government ended up losing the citizens' trust.
examples.note: The construction 'à force de + infinitive' expresses cumulative cause, equivalent to 'a fuerza de' in Spanish.

title: Narrativas personales complejas: matices temporales y perspectiva / Personal narratives with depth and perspective
bridge: In French, unlike Spanish, the use of the passé composé and the imparfait is stricter: the passé composé marks punctual or completed events, while the imparfait describes states, habits, or ongoing actions. Additionally, the conditionnel passé (aurais + past participle) is used in French to express unfulfilled hypotheses about the past, where Spanish often uses the pluperfect subjunctive ('hubiera hecho'). Be careful with temporal agreement in indirect speech: French requires more systematic tense shifts than Spanish.
rule: To narrate complex personal experiences in French at a C1 level, master: 1) The passé composé / imparfait opposition: use passé composé for punctual actions (Elle a frappé à la porte) and imparfait for descriptions or habits (Il faisait beau). 2) The plus-que-parfait (avais + past participle) for actions prior to another past action: Après que j'avais fini, je suis parti. 3) The conditionnel passé for counterfactual hypotheses: Si j'avais su, je serais venu (equivalent to Spanish 'Si hubiera sabido, habría venido'). 4) In indirect speech in the past, transform the tenses: present → imparfait, passé composé → plus-que-parfait, future → conditionnel présent. Example: Il a dit: «Je suis fatigué» → Il a dit qu'il était fatigué. 5) The subjunctive is used more sparingly than in Spanish; in French it is not used after 'après que' (indicative is required), whereas in Spanish 'después de que' can take the subjunctive. 6) To narrate with perspective, use expressions like 'avec le recul', 'en y repensant', 'réflexion faite' to indicate retrospective evaluation.

concept_examples.text: Avec le recul, je me rends compte que j'aurais dû accepter cette offre.
concept_examples.translation: With hindsight, I realize I should have accepted that offer.
concept_examples.phonetic: /avɛk lə ʁəkyl ʒə mə ʁɑ̃ kɔ̃t kə ʒ‿oʁɛ dy aksɛpte sɛt ɔfʁ/

concept_examples.text: Quand j'étais enfant, je passais mes étés chez ma grand-mère, mais un été, tout a changé.
concept_examples.translation: When I was a child, I used to spend my summers at my grandmother's house, but one summer everything changed.
concept_examples.phonetic: /kɑ̃ ʒ‿etɛz‿ɑ̃fɑ̃ ʒə pase me‿z‿ete ʃe ma ɡʁɑ̃mɛʁ mɛ œ̃n‿ete tu a ʃɑ̃ʒe/

concept_examples.text: Si j'avais su que tu venais, j'aurais préparé quelque chose de spécial.
concept_examples.translation: If I had known you were coming, I would have prepared something special.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si ʒ‿avɛ sy kə ty vənɛ ʒ‿ɔʁɛ pʁepaʁe kɛlkʃoz də spesjal/

concept_examples.text: Réflexion faite, je n'aurais jamais dû lui confier ce secret.
concept_examples.translation: On reflection, I never should have confided that secret in him.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʁeflɛksjɔ̃ fɛt ʒə n‿ɔʁɛ ʒamɛ dy lɥi kɔ̃fje sə səkʁɛ/

common_error.wrong: Après que je suis parti, elle m'a appelé.
common_error.correct: Après que je suis parti, elle m'a appelé.
common_error.correct_alt: Après que je fus parti, elle m'appela. (literary, passé antérieur)
common_error.explanation: This example is actually correct; however, a common error is using the subjunctive after 'après que' (influenced by Spanish). Saying 'Après que je sois parti' is incorrect; in French, the indicative is required. Another common mistake is using the imperfect for punctual actions: 'J'ai mangé quand il est arrivé' (correct) vs. 'Je mangeais quand il est arrivé' (implies an ongoing action). To avoid errors, remember that 'après que' requires the indicative and that the passé composé aims to mark completed events.

levels.label: Nuancer avec l'imparfait et le passé composé
levels.translation: Nuancing with the imperfect and passé composé

examples.original: Il pleuvait depuis des heures quand la nuit est tombée.
examples.phonetic: /il pləvɛ dəpɥi de‿z‿œʁ kɑ̃ la nɥi ɛ tɔ̃be/
examples.translation: It had been raining for hours when night fell.
examples.note: Use of the imperfect for an ongoing action and the passé composé for the punctual event.

examples.original: Je lui parlais doucement pendant qu'elle pleurait.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə lɥi paʁlɛ dusmɑ̃ pɑ̃dɑ̃ kɛl plœʁɛ/
examples.translation: I was speaking softly to her while she was crying.
examples.note: Both verbs in the imperfect to describe simultaneous ongoing actions in the past.

examples.original: Elle a terminé son discours, puis tout le monde a applaudi.
examples.phonetic: /ɛl a tɛʁmine sɔ̃ diskuʁ pɥi tu lə mɔ̃d a aploidi/
examples.translation: She finished her speech, and then everyone applauded.
examples.note: Passé composé for successive and completed actions.

levels.label: Hypothèses contrefactuelles avec le conditionnel passé
levels.translation: Counterfactual hypotheses with the conditional compound

examples.original: Sans ton aide, nous aurions échoué.
examples.phonetic: /sɑ̃ tɔ̃n‿ɛd nu z‿ɔʁjɔ̃ eʃwe/
examples.translation: Without your help, we would have failed.
examples.note: Structure: sans + noun, conditional compound for unrealized hypotheses.

examples.original: J'aurais aimé voyager davantage avant d'avoir des enfants.
examples.phonetic: /ʒ‿ɔʁɛ eme vwajaʒe davɑ̃taʒ avɑ̃ davwaʁ de‿z‿ɑ̃fɑ̃/
examples.translation: I would have liked to travel more before having children.
examples.note: Conditional compound to express regret or unfulfilled desire.

examples.original: Si tu étais arrivé plus tôt, nous serions partis à l'heure.
examples.phonetic: /si ty ɛtɛ aʁive ply to nu səʁjɔ̃ paʁti a l‿œʁ/
examples.translation: If you had arrived earlier, we would have left on time.
examples.note: The structure si + pluperfect, conditional compound is key for hypotheses.

levels.label: Discours indirect au passé et perspective rétrospective
levels.translation: Indirect speech in the past and retrospective perspective

examples.original: Elle m'a avoué qu'elle avait toujours voulu devenir écrivaine.
examples.phonetic: /ɛl m‿a avwe kɛl avɛ tuʒuʁ vuly dəvniʁ ekʁivɛn/
examples.translation: She confessed to me that she had always wanted to become a writer.
examples.note: Transformation: passé composé (a avoué) + imperfect (voulu) in indirect speech.

examples.original: En y repensant, je me dis que j'aurais dû écouter mon intuition.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ ni ʁəpɑ̃sɑ̃ ʒə mə di kə ʒ‿ɔʁɛ dy ekute mɔ̃n‿ɛ̃tɥisjɔ̃/
examples.translation: Thinking it over, I tell myself I should have listened to my intuition.
examples.note: Expression 'en y repensant' to add retrospective perspective.

examples.original: Il prétendait qu'il n'avait jamais vu ce film auparavant.
examples.phonetic: /il pʁetɑ̃dɛ kil n‿avɛ ʒamɛ vy sə film opaʁavɑ̃/
examples.translation: He claimed he had never seen that film before.
examples.note: Use of imperfect in the main verb and pluperfect for the prior action.

translations.en: Personal narratives with depth and perspective

title: Maîtriser la réfutation et l'argumentation avancée / Mastering advanced refutation and argumentation
bridge: In Spanish, when refuting, we often use connectors like 'sin embargo', 'no obstante' or 'si bien', and we often introduce the objection directly. In French, sophisticated refutation relies on more nuanced structures: the use of the subjunctive after concessive phrases such as 'bien que' or 'encore que', and the use of the conditional to soften statements (je dirais que, il faudrait considérer). Additionally, negation in French has complex constructions like 'ne... point', 'ne... que' (only) that can alter the nuance. Be careful not to fall into the trap of translating 'aunque' literally as 'bien que' without using the subjunctive, or using 'pour autant' as 'para tanto', when it actually means 'por eso' in negative contexts.
rule: For C1-level argumentation, mastering the nuances of concession and refutation is essential. Here are the key structures: 1) Concessive phrases that require the subjunctive: 'bien que', 'encore que', 'quoique' (although), 'sans que' (without). Example: 'Bien qu'il soit tard, nous continuons.' 2) Opposition connectors with the indicative: 'tandis que', 'alors que' (whereas), 'cependant', 'néanmoins' (however). 3) To refute politely, use the conditional: 'Je ne dirais pas cela', 'Il faudrait plutôt considérer que...' 4) The restrictive negation 'ne... que' (only) and 'ne... point' (literary form of 'no'), which can appear in formal conversation. 5) To reformulate the opponent's argument, use constructions like 'En d'autres termes', 'Pour être plus précis', 'Ce que vous dites revient à...'. 6) In direct refutation, the structure 'Certes..., mais...' (Admittedly..., but...) allows you to acknowledge a point before attacking it. Remember that the 'subjunctive' is key to sounding less categorical; in Spanish we use the indicative after 'aunque' when the fact is presented as certain, but in French, concession requires the subjunctive.

concept_examples.text: Bien que votre argument soit valable, il ne prend pas en compte les aspects économiques.
concept_examples.translation: Although your argument may be valid, it does not take economic aspects into account.
concept_examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə vɔ.tʁ‿aʁ.ɡy.mɑ̃ swa va.labl, il nə pʁɑ̃ pa.‿ɑ̃ kɔ̃t le.z‿as.pɛ e.kɔ.nɔ.mik/

concept_examples.text: Certes, la mondialisation a des avantages, mais elle accentue les inégalités.
concept_examples.translation: Admittedly, globalization has advantages, but it accentuates inequalities.
concept_examples.phonetic: /sɛʁ.tə, la mɔ̃.dja.li.za.sjɔ̃ a de.z‿a.vɑ̃.taʒ, mɛ ɛl.l‿ak.sɑ̃.tɥi le.z‿i.ne.ɡa.li.te/

concept_examples.text: Encore que ce ne soit pas tout à fait vrai, votre point de vue mérite réflexion.
concept_examples.translation: Even if it is not entirely true, your point of view deserves consideration.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃.kɔʁ kə sə nwa pa tu.t‿a fɛ vʁɛ, vɔ.tʁə pwɛ̃ də vy me.ʁit ʁe.flɛk.sjɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: Je ne dirais pas exactement cela; je reformulerais plutôt votre idée.
concept_examples.translation: I wouldn’t say exactly that; rather, I would rephrase your idea.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə di.ʁɛ pa ɛɡ.zak.tə.mɑ̃ sə.la; ʒə ʁə.fɔʁ.my.lə.ʁɛ pʁy.to vɔ.tʁ‿i.de/

common_error.wrong: Bien que ton argument est valable, je ne suis pas d'accord.
common_error.correct: Bien que ton argument soit valable, je ne suis pas d'accord.
common_error.correct_alt: Quoique ton argument soit valable, je ne suis pas d'accord.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, 'aunque' is followed by the indicative when the fact is presented as real ('aunque es válido', 'aunque está lloviendo'). In French, concessive conjunctions such as 'bien que', 'quoique', and 'encore que' always require the subjunctive (whether the fact is real or hypothetical). Using the indicative is perceived as a B2-level error. The solution is to learn the phrases that trigger the subjunctive: bien que, quoique, encore que, sans que, à moins que (unless).

examples.original: Bien qu'elle soit compétente, elle manque d'expérience.
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ k‿ɛl swa kɔ̃.pe.tɑ̃t, ɛl mɑ̃k d‿ɛk.spe.ʁjɑ̃s/
examples.translation: Although she may be competent, she lacks experience.
examples.note: Use 'bien que' + subjunctive (soit), not 'est'. The concession is marked by the subjunctive.

examples.original: Encore que les chiffres soient élevés, ils sont fiables.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃.kɔʁ kə le ʃifʁ swa.t‿el.ve, il sɔ̃ fjabl/
examples.translation: Even if the figures are high, they are reliable.
examples.note: 'Encore que' is more formal than 'bien que' and is used with the subjunctive. It often appears in academic registers.

examples.original: Sans que vous le remarquiez, il a changé d'avis.
examples.phonetic: /sɑ̃ kə vu lə ʁə.maʁ.kje, il a ʃɑ̃.ʒe d‿a.vi/
examples.translation: Without you noticing, he changed his mind.
examples.note: 'Sans que' requires the subjunctive and expresses an unnoticed condition. In Spanish, 'sin que' + subjunctive is used (though sometimes the indicative is used in informal speech).

examples.original: Tandis que vous prétendez que la solution est simple, elle requiert une analyse approfondie.
examples.phonetic: /tɑ̃.di kə vu pʁe.tɑ̃d kə la sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ ɛ sɛ̃pl, ɛl ʁə.kjɛʁ yn.n‿a.na.li.z‿a.pʁɔ.fɔ̃.di/
examples.translation: Whereas you claim the solution is simple, it requires in-depth analysis.
examples.note: Use 'tandis que' + indicative to contrast two facts. Do not confuse it with 'pendant que' (while).

examples.original: Votre argument repose sur une prémisse erronée. Autrement dit, il est invalide.
examples.phonetic: /vɔ.tʁ‿aʁ.ɡy.mɑ̃ ʁə.poz syʁ yn pʁe.mis e.ʁɔ.ne. o.tʁə.mɑ̃ di, il ɛ.t‿ɛ̃.va.lid/
examples.translation: Your argument is based on a flawed premise. In other words, it is invalid.
examples.note: 'Autrement dit' (in other words) is a key tool for reformulation in debate.

examples.original: Je conçois votre point de vue, néanmoins il ne me convainc pas.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə kɔ̃.swa vɔ.tʁə pwɛ̃ də vy, ne.ɑ̃.mwa.n‿il nə mə kɔ̃.vɛ̃ pɑ/
examples.translation: I understand your point of view, nevertheless it does not convince me.
examples.note: 'Néanmoins' is a formal opposition connector. It can be replaced by 'cependant' or 'toutefois'.

levels.label: Réfutation avec le conditionnel et la négation restrictive
levels.translation: Refutation with conditional and restrictive negation

examples.original: Je ne prétendrais pas que tout est perdu, mais nous devons réagir.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə pʁe.tɑ̃.dʁɛ pɑ kə tu.t‿ɛ pɛʁ.dy, mɛ nu də.vɔ̃ ʁe.a.ʒiʁ/
examples.translation: I wouldn’t claim that everything is lost, but we must react.
examples.note: The conditional (prétendrais) softens the statement and shows openness. It is typical of academic registers.

examples.original: Cette politique ne fait qu'accroître les inégalités.
examples.phonetic: /sɛt pɔ.li.tik nə fɛ k‿a.kʁwatʁ le.z‿i.ne.ɡa.li.te/
examples.translation: This policy does nothing but increase inequalities.
examples.note: 'Ne... que' = 'only' with a restrictive meaning. Do not confuse it with simple negation 'ne... pas'.

examples.original: Je ne vois point de solution à ce problème dans votre proposition.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə vwa pwɛ̃ də sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ a sə pʁɔ.blɛm dɑ̃ vɔ.tʁə pʁɔ.po.zi.sjɔ̃/
examples.translation: I see no solution to this problem in your proposal.
examples.note: The literary form 'ne... point' is more emphatic than 'ne... pas' and is used in formal debates to add a categorical nuance.

title: Vocabulaire académique spécialisé / Academic specialized vocabulary
bridge: In academic French, Latin or Greek terms often have a more restricted and formal use than in Spanish. For example, while in Spanish 'abordar' is used in both colloquial and academic contexts, in French 'aborder' is more specific to formal and academic discourse. Additionally, false friends like 'actuellement' (actually, not currently) or 'évidence' (evidence, but also 'obviousness') can distort the meaning of your arguments. Pay close attention to the specific collocations required by these terms.
rule: In C1 academic French, precise use of nominalizations (e.g., 'la mise en évidence' instead of 'démontrer'), discourse connectors (e.g., 'en dépit de', 'nonobstant', 'dans la mesure où'), and analytical verbs (e.g., 'inférer', 'corroborer', 'nuancer') is expected. The subjunctive is used in subordinate clauses after impersonal expressions or verbs of doubt, but the infinitive or indicative is often preferred in formal contexts when the subject is the same (e.g., 'Il convient de noter que...' vs. 'Il est essentiel que l'on note...'). Nuances between academic synonyms are important: 'démontrer' implies proof, 'montrer' is more general, 'prouver' is used in scientific contexts, and 'mettre en évidence' emphasizes the process. Nominalizations and passive constructions (with 'il est + adjective + de') are common to maintain impersonality. Typical errors include using 'actual' for 'actuel' (which means 'current' in the sense of 'present,' not 'real'), 'évidemment' for 'evidentemente' (but in French it can also mean 'of course'), and not using the correct preposition after certain verbs like 'consister à' (not 'en' for actions).

concept_examples.text: Dans cette dissertation, nous allons aborder la problématique de la mondialisation sous un angle interdisciplinaire.
concept_examples.translation: En esta disertación, vamos a abordar la problemática de la globalización desde un ángulo interdisciplinario.
concept_examples.phonetic: /dɑ̃ sɛt disɛʁtasjɔ̃, nu z‿alɔ̃ abɔʁde la pʁɔblematik də la mɔ̃dializasjɔ̃ su z‿œ̃n‿ɑ̃ɡl ɛ̃tɛʁdisiplinɛʁ/

concept_examples.text: L'étude corrobore les hypothèses antérieures tout en nuançant certains résultats.
concept_examples.translation: El estudio corrobora las hipótesis anteriores a la vez que matiza ciertos resultados.
concept_examples.phonetic: /letyd kɔʁɔbɔʁ le ipotɛz ɑ̃teʁjœʁ tu ɑ̃ nyɑ̃sɑ̃ sɛʁtɛ̃ ʁezylta/

concept_examples.text: Il convient de souligner que la fiabilité de ces données reste à vérifier.
concept_examples.translation: Conviene subrayar que la fiabilidad de estos datos está por verificar.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il kɔ̃vjɛ̃ də suliɲe kə la fjabilite də se dɔne ʁɛst a veʁifje/

concept_examples.text: En dépit des limites méthodologiques, cette approche offre des perspectives prometteuses.
concept_examples.translation: A pesar de las limitaciones metodológicas, este enfoque ofrece perspectivas prometedoras.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ depi de limit metodolɔʒik, sɛt apʁɔʃ ɔfʁ de pɛʁspɛktiv pʁɔmɛtøz/

common_error.wrong: J'étudie actuellement les changements climatiques, donc je suis actif dans le débat académique.
common_error.correct: J'étudie actuellement les changements climatiques, donc je suis engagé dans le débat académique.
common_error.correct_alt: Je me consacre actuellement à l'étude des changements climatiques, donc je participe activement au débat académique.
common_error.explanation: The error here is the use of 'actif', which in French means 'active' in the sense of 'performing an action,' but it does not sound natural in an academic context; typically, 'engagé' (committed) or 'impliqué' (involved) is used instead. Additionally, the false friend 'actuellement' means 'currently,' not 'actually.' Spanish speakers tend to confuse 'actif' with 'actualizado' or 'real,' but it does not have that meaning in French. It is important to use specific academic collocations.

examples.original: Cette étude démontre une corrélation significative entre les variables.
examples.phonetic: /sɛt etyd demɔ̃tʁ yn kɔʁelasjɔ̃ siɲifikativ ɑ̃tʁ le vaʁjabl/
examples.translation: Este estudio demuestra una correlación significativa entre las variables.
examples.note: We use 'démontrer' when there is conclusive evidence. Do not confuse it with 'montrer' (to show), which is more general.

examples.original: Nous pouvons inférer que la politique a influencé les résultats.
examples.phonetic: /nu puvɔ̃ z‿ɛ̃feʁe kə la pɔlitik a ɛ̃flyɑ̃se le ʁezylta/
examples.translation: Podemos inferir que la política influyó en los resultados.
examples.note: 'Inférer' is a formal verb meaning 'to deduce.' It is used in academic contexts and is constructed with 'que' + indicative.

examples.original: Il faut nuancer cette affirmation car elle est trop générale.
examples.phonetic: /il fo nyɑ̃se sɛt afiʁmasjɔ̃ kaʁ ɛl ɛ tʁo ʒeneʁal/
examples.translation: Hay que matizar esta afirmación porque es demasiado general.
examples.note: 'Nuancer' is key to expressing nuances in academic debate; it is often used in the impersonal infinitive form.

examples.original: En dépit de ces obstacles, nous maintenons notre position.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ depi de se ɔpstakəl, nu mɛ̃tənɔ̃ nɔtʁ pozisjɔ̃/
examples.translation: A pesar de estos obstáculos, mantenemos nuestra posición.
examples.note: 'En dépit de' is more formal than 'malgré' and is used in academic and literary registers.

examples.original: Nonobstant les critiques, l'approche reste viable.
examples.phonetic: /nɔ̃ɔbstɑ̃ le kʁitik, l‿apʁɔʃ ʁɛst vjabl/
examples.translation: No obstante las críticas, el enfoque sigue siendo viable.
examples.note: 'Nonobstant' is extremely formal and is mainly used in legal or academic texts; it can be replaced by 'malgré' in less formal contexts.

examples.original: Dans la mesure où les données sont fiables, nous pouvons conclure.
examples.phonetic: /dɑ̃ la məzyʁ u le dɔne sɔ̃ fjabl, nu puvɔ̃ kɔ̃klyʁ/
examples.translation: En la medida en que los datos son fiables, podemos concluir.
examples.note: This connector expresses a justified condition or cause, very useful in academic argumentation.

examples.original: La mise en évidence de ces phénomènes est cruciale pour la recherche.
examples.phonetic: /la miz ɑ̃ evidɑ̃s də se fenɔmɛn ɛ kʁysjal puʁ la ʁəʃɛʁʃ/
examples.translation: La puesta en evidencia de estos fenómenos es crucial para la investigación.
examples.note: The phrase 'mise en évidence' is preferred over 'démonstration' to emphasize the process of evidencing.

examples.original: Il est essentiel que l'on examine les implications éthiques.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛt‿esɑ̃sjɛl kə l‿ɔ̃ ɛgzamin le ɛ̃plikasjɔ̃ etik/
examples.translation: Es esencial que examinemos las implicaciones éticas.
examples.note: The subjunctive is mandatory after 'il est essentiel que.' It can also be used with 'il est essentiel d'examiner' and the infinitive.

examples.original: Il s'avère que les résultats confirment notre hypothèse initiale.
examples.phonetic: /il savɛʁ kə le ʁezylta kɔ̃fiʁm nɔtʁ ipɔtɛz inisjal/
examples.translation: Resulta que los resultados confirman nuestra hipótesis inicial.
examples.note: The impersonal 'il s'avère que' is an academic alternative to 'resulta que' and adds objectivity.

title: Langage familier et expressions idiomatiques / Colloquial language and idioms
bridge: In French, colloquial language is very rich and often differs from the standard register in pronunciation (such as the dropping of 'ne' in negation: 'je ne sais pas' becomes 'chais pas') and in the use of idiomatic expressions that do not have a direct equivalent in Spanish. Unlike Spanish, where many colloquial expressions vary widely between countries, colloquial French in France is quite homogeneous and is characterized by the use of 'verlan' (syllable inversion, like 'meuf' from 'femme') and particles like 'quoi' at the end of sentences. Be careful: although some expressions seem similar to Spanish (such as 'tomar el pelo' vs 'se moquer de quelqu'un'), they often have different nuances.
rule: In French, colloquial register is distinguished by: 1) The omission of the particle 'ne' in negation (e.g. 'je sais pas' instead of 'je ne sais pas'), though in formal writing it should be kept. 2) The use of 'on' for 'nous' (e.g. 'on va' instead of 'nous allons'). 3) Verlan, which inverts syllables: 'fou' → 'ouf', 'femme' → 'meuf', 'truc' → 'keum' (though the latter is less common). 4) Idiomatic expressions such as 'avoir la flemme' (to be lazy), 'être crevé' (to be exhausted), 'casser les pieds' (to annoy), 'coûter un bras' (to cost an arm and a leg). 5) The use of 'quoi' as a filler word at the end of sentences to emphasize or seek confirmation. 6) The elision of the 'e' in 'je' before verbs starting with a consonant (e.g. 'j'peux' instead of 'je peux'), though it is recommended to use this only in very informal contexts. 7) The use of the interrogative 't' instead of 'est-ce que' (e.g. 'tu viens t'?' instead of 'est-ce que tu viens?'). At C1 level, you should recognize and understand these forms when listening, but use them sparingly and according to the social context.

concept_examples.text: Chais pas, moi, j'en ai marre de ce taf.
concept_examples.translation: I don't know, I'm sick of this job.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃɛ pɑ mwa ʒɑ̃nɛ maʁ də sə taf/

concept_examples.text: Ce film, il craint un max, non?
concept_examples.translation: This movie sucks big time, right?
concept_examples.phonetic: /sə film il kʁɛ̃ œ̃ maks nɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: T'as vu cette meuf? Elle est trop canon!
concept_examples.translation: Have you seen that chick? She's so hot!
concept_examples.phonetic: /ta vy sɛt mœf ɛl ɛ tʁo kanɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: On se fait un resto ce soir? J'ai la flemme de cuisiner.
concept_examples.translation: Shall we go out for dinner tonight? I can't be bothered to cook.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ sə fɛ œ̃ ʁɛsto sə swaʁ ʒɛ la flɛm də kɥizine/

common_error.wrong: Je suis fatigué, je ne peux pas venir, parce que j'ai beaucoup de travail.
common_error.correct: Je suis crevé, je peux pas venir, j'ai trop de boulot.
common_error.correct_alt: Je suis épuisé, je peux pas venir, j'ai un tas de travail.
common_error.explanation: The mistake is using a register that is too formal in a colloquial context. Spanish speakers tend to transfer the formal structure from standard Spanish, but in colloquial French, the 'ne' in negation is omitted, 'crevé' is used instead of 'fatigué', and 'boulot' instead of 'travail'. Also, the use of 'parce que' for subordination is avoided, and 'j'ai trop de' is used for emphasis. The key is to adapt the level of formality to the context: in a conversation between friends, the register should be more relaxed.

examples.original: C'est ouf, ce qu'il a fait!
examples.phonetic: /sɛ tuf sə kil a fɛ/
examples.translation: It's insane what he did!
examples.note: 'Ouf' is verlan for 'fou' (crazy). It is used to express amazement or disbelief.

examples.original: Je lui ai dit, mais elle s'en fout, la meuf.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə lɥi ɛ di mɛ ɛl sɑ̃ fu la mœf/
examples.translation: I told her, but she doesn't give a damn, that chick.
examples.note: 'Meuf' is verlan for 'femme' (woman). It is used colloquially to refer to a girl or woman.

examples.original: T'es trop cher, frérot.
examples.phonetic: /te tʁo ʃɛʁ fʁeʁo/
examples.translation: You're too expensive, bro.
examples.note: 'Frérot' is a diminutive of 'frère' (brother) and is used between friends as a vocative.

examples.original: J'ai un truc à te dire, mais c'est pas pour tout de suite.
examples.phonetic: /ʒɛ œ̃ tʁyk a tə diʁ mɛ sɛ pa puʁ tut də sɥit/
examples.translation: I've got something to tell you, but it's not for right now.
examples.note: 'Truc' is a generic word for 'thing', widely used in informal speech.

examples.original: Ah, je tombe de sommeil, je vais me coucher.
examples.phonetic: /a ʒə tɔ̃b də sɔmɛj ʒə vɛ mə kuʃe/
examples.translation: I'm falling asleep, I'm going to bed.
examples.note: Equivalent to 'me muero de sueño' in Spanish.

examples.original: Tu me casses les pieds avec tes questions!
examples.phonetic: /ty mə kas le pje avɛk te kɛstjɔ̃/
examples.translation: You're getting on my nerves with your questions!
examples.note: Equivalent to 'molestar' (to annoy), but more emphatic. It is used to express irritation.

examples.original: J'ai la dalle, je pourrais manger un cheval.
examples.phonetic: /ʒɛ la dal ʒə puʁɛ mɑ̃ʒe œ̃ ʃəval/
examples.translation: I'm so hungry I could eat a horse.
examples.note: Literally 'I have the iron', it is used to say 'I'm very hungry'.

examples.original: Il a la flemme de faire ses devoirs.
examples.phonetic: /il a la flɛm də fɛʁ se dəvwaʁ/
examples.translation: He can't be bothered to do his homework.
examples.note: Equivalent to 'tener pereza' or 'flojera' (to be lazy).

examples.original: Ben écoute, c'est comme ça, quoi.
examples.phonetic: /bɛ̃ ekut sɛ kɔm sa kwa/
examples.translation: Well listen, it's like this, you know?
examples.note: 'Ben' (short for 'eh bien') and 'quoi' are used as filler words to fill pauses and add emphasis.

examples.original: Franchement, il est relou, ce mec.
examples.phonetic: /fʁɑ̃ʃmɑ̃ il ɛ ʁəlu sə mɛk/
examples.translation: Frankly, he's such a pain, this guy.
examples.note: 'Relou' is verlan for 'lourd' (heavy), used to say someone is annoying.

examples.original: Bah, j'sais pas, moi, c'est toi qui vois.
examples.phonetic: /ba ʃɛ pɑ mwa sɛ twa ki vwa/
examples.translation: Well, I don't know, I guess you decide.
examples.note: The repetition of 'moi' emphasizes personal opinion. It is very common in informal speech.

examples.original: Eh, t'as vu? Il s'est encore garé en double file.
examples.phonetic: /e ta vy il sɛt ɑ̃kɔʁ ɡaʁe ɑ̃ dubl fil/
examples.translation: Hey, did you see? He parked in a no-parking zone again.
examples.note: 'T'as vu' is a contraction of 'tu as vu', very common in informal conversations to get attention.

title: Nuancer et argumenter à l'oral / Nuancing and orally arguing
bridge: In Spanish, to nuance we use connectors like 'la verdad es que', 'es que' or the subjunctive with 'aunque'. In French, formal speech requires more precise constructions such as 'certes… mais', 'il n'empêche que', 'encore que' and the use of the subjunctive after concessive phrases. The greatest danger for a Spanish speaker is to translate 'aunque' literally as 'bien que' (which requires the subjunctive) or to use 'malgré que' colloquially, when in careful register 'bien que' or 'encore que' are preferred.
rule: For C1-level argumentation, spoken French uses: 1) Concessive connectors: 'certes… mais', 'il est vrai que… mais', 'soit… mais' (with indicative); 'bien que', 'encore que', 'quoique' (always with subjunctive). 2) Opinion nuancers: 'à vrai dire', 'tout compte fait', 'en fin de compte', 'pour ma part'. 3) Structures to soften: 'je dirais que', 'il me semble que', 'j'aurais tendance à penser que' (conditional for politeness). 4) Reformulators: 'autrement dit', 'en d'autres termes', 'c'est-à-dire'. Exception: 'malgré que' is used colloquially, but standard French prefers 'bien que' + subjunctive. Note: 'encore que' is placed at the end of the sentence or after a pause, followed by the subjunctive. In spontaneous speech, 'enfin' is often used to soften or correct, but at C1 level more sophisticated markers are expected.

concept_examples.text: Certes, le projet est ambitieux, mais il reste réalisable.
concept_examples.translation: Ciertamente, el proyecto es ambicioso, pero sigue siendo realizable.
concept_examples.phonetic: sɛʁ.tɛ, lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.bi.sjø, mɛ il ʁɛst ʁe.a.li.zabl

concept_examples.text: Bien que je sois d'accord sur le principe, je doute de la mise en œuvre.
concept_examples.translation: Aunque estoy de acuerdo en el principio, dudo de la puesta en práctica.
concept_examples.phonetic: bjɛ̃ kə ʒə swa d‿a.kɔʁ syʁ lə pʁɛ̃.sip, ʒə dut də la miz‿ɑ̃ œvʁ

concept_examples.text: À vrai dire, je préfère la version initiale, tout compte fait.
concept_examples.translation: A decir verdad, prefiero la versión inicial, después de todo.
concept_examples.phonetic: a vʁɛ diʁ, ʒə pʁe.fɛʁ la vɛʁ.sjɔ̃ i.ni.sjal, tu kɔ̃t fɛ

concept_examples.text: Encore que ce soit discutable, son argument mérite réflexion.
concept_examples.translation: Aunque sea discutible, su argumento merece reflexión.
concept_examples.phonetic: ɑ̃.kɔʁ kə sə swa dis.ky.tabl, sɔ̃ aʁ.ɡy.mɑ̃ me.ʁit ʁe.flɛk.sjɔ̃

common_error.wrong: Malgré que je sois fatigué, je vais continuer.
common_error.correct: Bien que je sois fatigué, je vais continuer.
common_error.correct_alt: Je vais continuer, encore que je sois fatigué.
common_error.explanation: The error comes from translating 'aunque' literally as 'malgré que'. In standard French, 'malgré que' is considered incorrect (though used colloquially). You should use 'bien que', 'quoique' or 'encore que', all followed by the subjunctive. To avoid the mistake, remember that 'malgré' is followed by a noun (malgré ma fatigue), and to introduce a verbal clause, use concessive phrases with the subjunctive.

levels.label: Marqueurs de concession / Marcadores de concesión

examples.original: Certes, il a de l'expérience, mais ses méthodes sont dépassées.
examples.phonetic: sɛʁ.tɛ, il a də l‿ɛk.spe.ʁjɑ̃s, mɛ se me.tɔd sɔ̃ de.pa.se
examples.translation: Ciertamente, tiene experiencia, pero sus métodos están obsoletos.
examples.note: Use of 'certes... mais' to concede a point before counter-arguing. Common structure in oral debates.

examples.original: Bien qu'il pleuve, nous partirons comme prévu.
examples.phonetic: bjɛ̃ k‿il plœv, nu paʁ.ti.ʁɔ̃ kɔm pʁe.vy
examples.translation: Aunque llueva, saldremos como estaba previsto.
examples.note: Remember that 'bien que' always requires the subjunctive (pleuve). In Spanish we use 'aunque' with indicative or subjunctive.

examples.original: Quoique ce soit risqué, je tente le coup.
examples.phonetic: kwa kə sə swa ʁis.ke, ʒə tɑ̃t lə ku
examples.translation: Aunque sea arriesgado, lo intento.
examples.note: 'Quoique' is synonymous with 'bien que', but more formal. It can merge into 'quoi que' in some contexts.

levels.label: Nuancer son opinion / Matizar la opinión

examples.original: À vrai dire, je ne suis pas convaincu par cet argument.
examples.phonetic: a vʁɛ diʁ, ʒə nə sɥi pa kɔ̃.vɛ̃.ky paʁ sɛ.t‿aʁ.ɡy.mɑ̃
examples.translation: A decir verdad, no estoy convencido de este argumento.
examples.note: Use of 'à vrai dire' to introduce a sincere opinion, similar to 'la verdad es que' but more formal.

examples.original: J'aurais tendance à penser que c'est une erreur stratégique.
examples.phonetic: ʒ‿ɔ.ʁɛ tɑ̃.dɑ̃s a pɑ̃.se kə sɛ.t‿y.n‿e.ʁœʁ stʁa.te.ʒik
examples.translation: Tendería a pensar que es un error estratégico.
examples.note: The conditional 'j'aurais tendance' softens the judgment. In Spanish, 'tendería a' or 'me inclino a pensar' is used.

examples.original: Tout compte fait, je pense que tu as raison.
examples.phonetic: tu kɔ̃t fɛ, ʒə pɑ̃s kə ty a ʁɛ.zɔ̃
examples.translation: Después de todo, creo que tienes razón.
examples.note: Expression to conclude after considering pros and cons. Equivalent to 'al fin y al cabo'.

examples.original: Autrement dit, tu proposes de changer toute la stratégie ?
examples.phonetic: o.tʁə.mɑ̃ di, ty pʁɔ.poz də ʃɑ̃.ʒe tut la stʁa.te.ʒi
examples.translation: Dicho de otro modo, ¿propones cambiar toda la estrategia?
examples.note: Reformulator to clarify or summarize. In Spanish: 'en otras palabras'.

examples.original: Certes, c'est une option, encore que je doute de son efficacité.
examples.phonetic: sɛʁ.tɛ, sɛ.t‿y.n‿ɔp.sjɔ̃, ɑ̃.kɔʁ kə ʒə dut də sɔ̃ e.fi.ka.si.te
examples.translation: Ciertamente, es una opción, aunque dudo de su eficacia.
examples.note: 'Encore que' is placed after a pause and with the subjunctive. It adds a nuance of reservation.

examples.original: Il me semble que cette approche mérite d'être envisagée sérieusement.
examples.phonetic: il mə sɑ̃bl kə sɛ.t‿a.pʁɔʃ me.ʁit d‿ɛ.tʁ‿ɑ̃.vi.za.ʒe se.ʁjøz.mɑ̃
examples.translation: Me parece que este enfoque merece ser considerado seriamente.
examples.note: Softened opinion form with 'il me semble que' + indicative. In Spanish: 'me parece que'.

examples.original: En fin de compte, il faut trancher : soit on accepte, soit on décline.
examples.phonetic: ɑ̃ fɛ̃ də kɔ̃t, il fo tʁɑ̃.ʃe : swa.t‿ɔ̃ ak.sɛpt, swa.t‿ɔ̃ de.klin
examples.translation: En definitiva, hay que decidir: o aceptamos o declinamos.
examples.note: Structure 'soit... soit...' to present clear alternatives. Equivalent to 'o... o...'.
